newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds firm on tame U.S. inflation.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds firm on tame U.S. inflation.

text.p: 1500 GMT - Austrian bonds finished strongly higher on Tuesday after market sentiment was boosted by the release of lower-than-expected U.S. inflation data, widely seen as having reduced the risk of an imminent rise in U.S. rates.

"Inflationary dangers have been reduced. That makes us confident," said one trader, adding that early gains in U.S. trading on Tuesday were likely to spill over into further gains in Vienna on Wednesday.
* New 10 year benchmark 5.75 pct bond maturing July 2006 up 35 bps at 98.65 to yield 5.93 (5.98) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 99.15/25 to yield 5.865/85.
* Latest five-year 4.375 bond maturing February 2002 closed up 20 bps at 98.25 in bourse trade to yield 4.78 (4.83) pct, quoted post-market at 98.52/60 to yield 4.72/70 percent.
* Austrian bond future up 64 bps at 107.55 on turnover of 875 lots.
* 10-year spread over Germany up one bps at four bps, five-year spread up two at ten bps.
* Money market rates steady with three-month VIBOR a tad higher at 3.405 (3.400) and overnight money at 3.15/3.40. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
